title: Root Vegetables
description: Plants that primarily grow underground and are harvested for their roots. They often require loose, well-drained soil.

title: Leafy Greens
description: Vegetables grown for their edible leaves. These plants usually need consistent moisture and are often sensitive to heat.

title: Fruit Vegetables
description: These plants produce fruits that are consumed as vegetables. They typically need plenty of sunlight and regular watering.

title: Legumes
description: Plants that fix nitrogen in the soil, improving fertility. They are often grown in rotation with other crops to maintain soil health.

title: Herbs
description: Plants grown for their aromatic leaves and are often used in cooking and medicinal purposes. They can be grown in containers or in-ground.

title: Flowers
description: Plants grown primarily for their ornamental flowers. They can attract pollinators and beneficial insects or repel pests.

title: Vines and Climbers
description: Plants that require support to grow vertically. They are ideal for maximizing space in small gardens by growing upward.

title: Brassicas
description: Cool-season vegetables that are members of the cabbage family. They can be susceptible to pests like aphids and cabbage worms.

title: Bulbs and Tubers
description: Underground storage organs. They often require well-drained soil and are planted at specific times of the year for optimal growth.

title: Perennials
description: Plants that grow back every year without needing to be replanted. They are great for low-maintenance gardening and providing continuous harvests.

title: Medicinals and Aromatics
description: Plants that have medicinal properties or aromatic uses. They are often grown in separate beds or containers due to their specific needs and uses.

title: Cover Crops
description: Plants grown to cover the soil rather than for harvest. They help improve soil health, suppress weeds, and prevent erosion.

title: Companion Plants
description: Plants grown together to benefit each other, either by deterring pests, attracting beneficial insects, or enhancing growth.

title: Shade-Tolerant Plants
description: Plants that can thrive in shaded or partially shaded areas of the garden. They are ideal for spaces that do not receive full sun.

title: Pollinator Attractors
description: Plants specifically chosen to attract pollinators like bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds, enhancing the garden’s ecological balance.

title: Berry Bushes
description: Small fruit-bearing plants that produce berries. They often require acidic soil and consistent watering.
